name: Restricted stock units (RSUs)
title: Restricted stock units (RSUs): Income, Basis and Worked Example
description: An RSU is an employer’s promise to deliver shares or cash after conditions are met. In the supported stock-delivery case, wage income and later sale gain are separate tax events.
definition: An RSU is an employer’s promise to deliver shares or cash after conditions are met. In the supported stock-delivery case, wage income and later sale gain are separate tax events.
explanation: RSU withholding and final tax are different. In a 2026 illustration, 100 delivered shares at $50 create $5,000 wage income. With $1,100 federal withholding and $400 other allocated withholding, retained value is $3,500, or 70 shares at that same price.
formula: Delivery wages = gross shares × income-date FMV. Sale basis = shares sold × FMV already included as wages. Capital gain = net sale proceeds − allocated basis.
formulaNote: U.S. 2026 stock-settled RSU delivery with simultaneous vesting/income recognition and no purchase price, or a single 2026 sale of an already-taxed nonrestricted lot. Optional federal supplemental method or entered actual withholding; other withholding and marginal tax rates are supplied assumptions. No payroll/FICA/state-law engine, deferred/private-company special timing, 83(i), wash sale, full return or final tax determination.

example.title: Separate wage value from retained shares equivalent
example.intro: settlement: 2026-11-24; shares: 100; fmv: 50; method: 2026 optional supplemental method; prior_supplemental: 0; actual_federal: 1100; other_withholding: 400; assumed_federal_rate: 32
steps: Optional federal withholding at 22% is 1,100. Add the entered 400 other withholding.
Retained value = 5,000 − 1,500 = 3,500; 3,500 / 50 = 70 shares equivalent. This is not broker rounding.
example.answer: Value after allocated withholding: 3,500.00 for the stated assumptions.
example.assumptions: U.S. 2026 stock-settled RSU delivery with simultaneous vesting/income recognition and no purchase price, or a single 2026 sale of an already-taxed nonrestricted lot. Optional federal supplemental method or entered actual withholding; other withholding and marginal tax rates are supplied assumptions. No payroll/FICA/state-law engine, deferred/private-company special timing, 83(i), wash sale, full return or final tax determination.

pitfall.title: Separate compensation from capital gain
pitfall.text: The grant price and the value remaining after withholding are not the income-date basis of the gross shares. Do not tax the same wage amount again as sale gain or mistake optional federal withholding for final tax.

tools.text: Restore the worked example and inspect the income/basis bridge.

name: Employee stock purchase plan (ESPP)
title: Employee stock purchase plan (ESPP): Income, Basis and Worked Example
description: A Section 423 ESPP lets eligible employees purchase employer shares under a qualifying plan. A later disposition can produce ordinary compensation and a separate capital gain or loss.
definition: A Section 423 ESPP lets eligible employees purchase employer shares under a qualifying plan. A later disposition can produce ordinary compensation and a separate capital gain or loss.
explanation: A Section 423 ESPP sale can contain both compensation and capital gain. In the stated qualifying-date example, 100 shares bought for $68 have $1,500 compensation and $8,300 adjusted basis; selling at $120 with $10 fees leaves $3,690 capital gain.
formula: Adjusted basis = purchase cost + compensation included in income. Capital result = net sale proceeds − adjusted basis. Compensation + capital result = economic gain/loss before tax.
formulaNote: One U.S. 2026 sale of a confirmed Section 423 ESPP lot, with exercise and nonrestricted share transfer together. Actual purchase/grant-date-as-if prices or a stated 0–15% discount formula; ordinary compensation, adjusted basis and separate capital term. Entered tax rates are assumptions. No plan/employment qualification, $25,000 accrual test, nonqualified plan, ISO, deferral, gift/death, wash sale, tax return or filing.

example.title: Keep the lookback purchase price distinct from the grant-date price
example.intro: plan: Section 423 plan confirmed; grant: 2023-12-01; purchase: 2024-06-01; sale: 2026-11-24; shares: 100; grant_fmv: 100; purchase_fmv: 80; sale_price: 120; fees: 10; ordinary_rate: 32; short_rate: 32; long_rate: 15; paid: 68; grant_option: 85
steps: Actual price is 68, while grant-date as-if exercise price is 85 against grant FMV 100.
Qualifying compensation per share = min(100 − 85, 120 − 68) = 15. For 100 shares this is 1,500.
Basis = 6,800 + 1,500 = 8,300. Net proceeds 11,990 less basis gives 3,690 capital gain.
example.answer: Capital gain / loss after compensation basis: 3,690.00 for the stated assumptions.
example.assumptions: One U.S. 2026 sale of a confirmed Section 423 ESPP lot, with exercise and nonrestricted share transfer together. Actual purchase/grant-date-as-if prices or a stated 0–15% discount formula; ordinary compensation, adjusted basis and separate capital term. Entered tax rates are assumptions. No plan/employment qualification, $25,000 accrual test, nonqualified plan, ISO, deferral, gift/death, wash sale, tax return or filing.

expected.label: Capital gain / loss after compensation basis

pitfall.title: Separate compensation from capital gain
pitfall.text: A disqualifying ESPP sale can have wage income despite an economic loss, or can have long-term capital gain if only the grant-date test fails. Do not apply the ISO sale-gain cap or the RSU withholding formula to Section 423 compensation.
